title: Delete a node with one child from a binary search tree
summary: To delete a node of degree 1, redirect its parent’s reference to the target’s only child.
context: Delete node 2 from a tree rooted at 8 containing values 2 through 15. The starting tree is the result of deleting node 1 in Figure 7-19. Node 2 has only a right child, 3. Two panels with a degree-1 check show the tree before and after deletion. The table compares their links. “Removed” means the node is no longer in the tree.
result: The remaining values 3 through 15 preserve search tree order. The operation redirects a link: the original node 3 becomes the left child of 4. It does not overwrite the value in node 2.

frames.title: Delete a node with one child from a binary search tree
frames.explanation: Follow 8 → 4 → 2 to find cur = 2 with parent pre = 4. Node 2 has no left child and one right child 3, so its degree is 1. Clearing 4.left as for a leaf would make node 3 unreachable from the root. Instead, pre.left = cur.right makes 4.left point to 3.

prose.title: Delete a node with one child from a binary search tree
prose.summary: To delete a node of degree 1, redirect its parent’s reference to the target’s only child.
context: Delete node 2 from a tree rooted at 8 containing values 2 through 15. The starting tree is the result of deleting node 1 in Figure 7-19. Node 2 has only a right child, 3. Two panels with a degree-1 check show the tree before and after deletion. The table compares their links. “Removed” means the node is no longer in the tree.
description: Animation steps 1 and 2 correspond to the two before-deletion columns in the links table. The last step corresponds to the two after-deletion columns. Look up any node by its row header in either state.
prose.result: The remaining values 3 through 15 preserve search tree order. The operation redirects a link: the original node 3 becomes the left child of 4. It does not overwrite the value in node 2.

steps.title: Locate target 2 and parent 4
steps.explanation: Target 2 is less than 8 and 4. Follow 8→4→2 to find cur=2 and pre=4. Node 4 has left child 2 and right child 6, and 2 has no left child and has right leaf 3. Nothing is deleted yet. For all links see the two before-deletion columns in “Binary search tree links before and after deleting a node with one child.”
steps.key_state: With cur = 2 and pre = 4, node 3 is still the right child of 2.
steps.announcement: Follow the left branch to find target 2 and parent 4.

steps.title: Confirm that 3 is the only child
steps.explanation: The check confirms degree 1 for cur (2): its only child is 3 on the right. Deletion must reconnect 3 to the parent; clearing 4.left would lose it. Only the check is complete: pre=4, and 4 still has left child 2 and right child 6, while 2 still has right child 3. The two before-deletion columns still describe the whole tree.
steps.key_state: Node 2 has degree 1 with sole right child 3. It is still the left child of parent 4 and has not been deleted.
steps.announcement: Confirm that target 2 has only one child, 3 on its right.

steps.title: Reconnect node 3 to the parent
steps.explanation: Execute pre.left = cur.right. Link 4.left now points directly to 3, bypassing and detaching 2. The root is still 8. Node 4 has left leaf 3 and right child 6, with all other links unchanged and values 3 through 15 retained. The two after-deletion columns mark node 2 as removed. Only a reference changed; node 3 is the original object.
steps.key_state: 4.left = 3. After deletion, 4 has left child 3 and right child 6. Node 2 has been detached.
steps.announcement: Attach the only child 3 to the left of parent 4, completing the deletion of node 2.
